title: Driven Harmonic Oscillator Physics Simulation
full_prompt:
Create a Manim scene named `DrivenHarmonicOscillator` that visualizes a physical simulation of a driven harmonic oscillator. The visualization must include three custom components:

1. A `Spring` class (inheriting from `VMobject`) that represents a 3D-like helical spring. It should construct a helix using a parametric curve, add straight lead lines at both ends, and use updaters to dynamically stretch, scale, and position itself between a fixed anchor point and a moving mass.

2. A `HarmonicOscillator` class (inheriting from `TrueDot` or a 3D dot) that simulates physical motion. It must maintain state variables for mass, damping, spring constant $k$, velocity, and external forces. It should use a sub-stepped numerical integration method (e.g., Euler-Cromer or Verlet) inside a frame-rate independent updater (`update_position(dt)`) to calculate displacement and acceleration based on Hooke's law, damping, and any registered external driving forces.

3. A `DynamicPlot` class (inheriting from `VMobject`) that dynamically plots the displacement of the oscillator over time on a set of axes.

In the main scene, set up the physical system with a fixed anchor point, a spring, and the oscillator mass. Apply a periodic external driving force (e.g., a sinusoidal force) to demonstrate driven harmonic motion, showing resonance or phase lag. Simultaneously, display a scrolling real-time plot of the mass's displacement over time.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Numerical instability in physics integration loop
common_failure_modes.note: If dt is too large or sub-stepping is not implemented, the mass will fly off-screen due to accumulated integration errors.
Using standard scaling instead of stretching along a single axis and repositioning can cause the spring's helix radius to distort.
The spring, mass, and plot updaters must execute in the correct order or within the same frame step to prevent visual separation.
